court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
claim_type: Fashion Nova's e-commerce website inaccessible to blind screen reader users; missing alt text on product images
outcome: Class action settlement — $5,150,000 total; California class members receive up to $4,000 per household; DOJ filed statement of interest opposing settlement as insufficient (Feb 2026); evidentiary hearing set March 30, 2026
estimated_defense_cost: Over $2.43M in class member distributions plus attorney fees on top; total exposure $5.15M+

summary_one_line: Largest disclosed ADA web accessibility class settlement in recent years at $5.15M — and the DOJ intervened in 2026 to argue even this wasn't enough, signaling elevated federal scrutiny.
notes: DOJ Statement of Interest filed February 2, 2026 argued the settlement's injunctive relief (a single sentence requiring site modifications) lacked monitoring or enforcement. DOJ argued settlement 'provided little value to most blind class members' while attorneys received disproportionate fees. Court set evidentiary hearing March 30, 2026. This case signals increasing DOJ scrutiny of hollow settlements — highly relevant for framing why structural compliance matters over quick settlements.
